issue.title: Instagram using generated tracking parameters?
issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

I noticed recently that I've been seeing Instagram links from friends where there's a clear tracking parameter, but instead of the usual `igshid`, `igsh`, or `igsi` name, the parameter has some random-looking four character name. In the past couple days alone I've seen `psln`, `srtk`, and `exln`. Earlier I've also observed `stkn` and `vrfl`. The value for each is always 12-13 bytes encoded as base64.

I didn't see these parameters in the [specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/master/TrackParamFilter/sections/specific.txt) list or anyone else reporting this phenomenon, so I wanted to give a head up that they may be encoding/randomizing their tracking parameters. Given that Instagram is a huge platform (and Meta a notorious tracker), I thought you'd want to know.

### Proposed solution

This is more of a heads up than a specific feature request. The way to address this depends highly on the pattern in the parameters. It may not be worth overcomplicating the matching rules. If it's always 4 lowercase letters, though, it looks like you could use a regex to match them. If that's too broad, you can restrict it to certain paths (I've only seen these on `/reel/` urls).

### Additional information

_No response_
